objective: Add low-cost first-frame Community video posters for previously viewed feed clips, without creating offscreen players or changing media storage, signed URL access, playback, ads, native dependencies, or package identity.
productionBaselineEvidence: verified: Android Production OTA run #248 published source SHA 11cf6bd096054dbf8ac204186b199fc835e740e3 on runtime 1.3.2. Current main @ 99cf163691a1cb1e24b3994c3bd44da3ee546a33 is the DEV baseline for this work and is NOT represented as the live production source. No production artifact or runtime is changed by this PR.
chosenApproach: Generate one bounded first-frame thumbnail from an already-mounted native player after a video becomes visible; keep an 18-item LRU cache keyed by the durable URL path; show cached posters in inactive feed cards.
selectionRationale: Avoid hidden players and speculative downloads for every feed item while replacing blank inactive video tiles with a useful preview after first viewing.
preserveBehaviors: No offscreen video players or speculative video downloads
Existing single-player lifecycle and autoplay/viewability behavior
Signed URL refresh and bounded playback retry
Fullscreen video sizing and saved playback position
Google IMA ads, companion placements and ad events
Video cache budget and weak-network fallback
No backend, RLS, storage, native dependency, package identity or production runtime changes
acceptanceChecks: Poster generation is deduplicated per durable media URL
Signed URL query rotation reuses the same poster cache entry
Poster cache remains bounded to 18 entries
Only native players already mounted for visible playback generate thumbnails
Inactive cards display cached poster with readable play affordance
Poster failure never blocks or breaks video playback
Web never calls the native thumbnail API
Focused poster tests, existing media regression suite, TypeScript and engineering gates pass
Physical-device visual, memory and weak-network verification remains an RC gate
alternativeApproaches: Mount hidden players for all feed videos (rejected: speculative downloads and native decoder/memory pressure).
Add a backend thumbnail pipeline now (rejected for this isolated client-side workstream; requires separately verified storage, migration, and upload lifecycle changes).
Replace expo-video or add a native module (rejected: unnecessary runtime and compatibility risk).
